rv.q: Never less than abundantly creative, funny and musically dextrous, Kathy and Stella's exploits will absolutely slay you.
Brittain and Fabian Aloise’s production is a shot of rock’n’roll escapism that capitalises on our collective fixation with true crime.
If you like Steve Martin’s cosy-slaughter TV series Only Murders in the Building — developed at about the same time — you’ll have plenty of fun here.
It arrives in the West End expanded from its original shorter format and has perhaps lost some of its charm in the process.
Kathy and Stella left me dead inside.
This show is an absolute smash-hit and deserves to be nominated for all the awards.
The show makes few demands of the audience but it has terrific comic integrity and a wonderful sense of fun.
All in all, it amounts to a killer addition to the musical pantheon.
This 2022. Edinburgh Fringe hit looks right at home in the West End beside the likes of Operation Mincemeat, Two Strangers, and Standing at the Sky’s Edge.
Bronté Barbé and Rebekah Hinds as Kathy and Stella respectively have terrific chemistry; their little jokes, cultural references and mannerisms are those of a long term friendship.

This works to an extent, especially because the musical numbers are so powerful and capable of delivering more emotion than the rather frothy story, but it also gave me a nagging sense of the show’s promise not quite being fulfilled.
This could be heading that way.
A hit at Edinburgh, Kathy and Stella now joins other shows (Operation Mincemeat, Two Strangers) bringing a smaller-scale but cheerful energy to the West End.

cn.t: Critics largely embrace this frothy true-crime musical spoof as a "daft and delightful" romp with catchy songs and winning leads, praising its clever satire of podcast culture. A few dismiss it as "oafish" and "slapdash," but most find it wildly fun escapism.
